title: Effects of Prolonged Exposure to Second-hand Smoke
what_it_is: Effects of Prolonged Exposure to Second-hand Smoke

sections.label: Second-hand smoke health effects
sections.summary: Second-hand smoke is linked to health conditions similar to smokers', and tobacco use causes about 7% of Singapore's disease burden, with six deaths daily.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Exposure to environmental tobacco smoke, also known as second-hand smoke, is associated with health conditions similar to those faced by smokers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: These include eye, nose and throat irritation, increased risk of respiratory infections, worsening of pre-existing respiratory problems, such as asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: And also, increased risk of heart disease, stroke and some cancers, such as breast and lung cancer.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: At the population level, the Global Burden of Disease 2016 study estimates that tobacco use contributes to approximately 7% of the total disease burden in Singapore, of which 1% is due to second-hand smoke and 6% due to active smoking.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: From the same study, six persons die each day from active smoking or exposure to second-hand smoke.

sections.label: MOH tobacco reduction approach
sections.summary: MOH will keep monitoring tobacco use effects and continue its multi-pronged approach to reduce tobacco use prevalence in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Health (MOH) will continue to monitor the effects of tobacco use and press on with its multi-pronged approach to reduce the prevalence of tobacco use in Singapore.

sections.label: HPB environmental tobacco smoke resources
sections.summary: HPB has developed online and print resources, such as brochures and posters, to raise awareness on environmental tobacco smoke.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: Currently, the Health Promotion Board (HPB) has developed online and print resources, for example, brochures, posters, to raise awareness on environmental tobacco smoke.

sections.label: Singapore statistics unavailable
sections.summary: A speaker asks whether Singapore statistics exist, and apologises for not having the exact numbers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: So, I am just wondering whether we have the statistics for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: I apologise, I do not have the exact numbers.
